summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and biliary cirrhosis was admitted with recurrent right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fever, consistent with cholangitis. She had recently completed a course of ciprofloxacin and started rifaximin but developed persistent symptoms. Imaging showed a stable 6 mm echogenic focus in the porta hepatis, possibly a stone or clip, with no biliary dilation. She was treated with IV meropenem, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged to complete a two-week course of ertapenem, followed by rifaximin, ciprofloxacin, and doxycycline for prophylaxis. A local reaction at the Pneumovax injection site was noted and documented as an allergy. Chronic conditions were managed, and she was stable at discharge.
